question: Should OpenClaw Core permanently own a durable Pi→Review→squash-promotion workflow and its vendored process-boundary contracts, or should this workflow live with the owner services/plugin surface behind a smaller generic Core seam?
rationale: The answer determines the long-term Core API, persistence, supply-chain owner, and operational support boundary; it cannot safely be inferred from passing focused tests.

options.title: Keep the workflow outside Core
options.body: Move the Pi/Review/promotion-specific contracts and orchestration to their owner service or plugin, retaining only a generic, narrowly documented Core capability if needed.

options.title: Sponsor a Core platform workflow
options.body: Explicitly approve the new Core product boundary, name its operational owner and contract publication process, then require upgrade and real integration proof before merge.

options.title: Pause the proposal
options.body: Close or defer this branch until a durable platform-orchestration product design is accepted.

recommendation.title: Keep the workflow outside Core
recommendation.body: Move the Pi/Review/promotion-specific contracts and orchestration to their owner service or plugin, retaining only a generic, narrowly documented Core capability if needed.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision changes the repository-wide Core ownership boundary and persisted workflow contract.
